purpose: Teach: じゅん/素子/すぅ/稔/ヤマト/松子/春日/立花

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんがお友達のじゅんさんと釣りに行かれた
lines.en: Gran, when Dad was young, he'd go fishing with his friend Jun.
lines.style: Soft, gazing inward. Measured pace, as if retrieving a memory from deep water. Tender nostalgia without sadness. Voice trails slightly on the final word.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん、お祖父ちゃん、若い頃、お姉様の素子さんとよく話されたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Yes, dear — and when Grandpa was young, he used to talk so much with my older sister Motoko, didn't he?
lines.style: Warm, gently testing. A light lilt at the end — playful reminder of something shared. Affectionate but observant, like she's watching him remember.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんが寝るとき「すぅ」と寝息を立てられた
lines.en: Gran, when Dad was young, he'd sleep making that little "suu" sound when he breathed.
lines.style: Quiet, almost reverent. Slight smile in the voice at the memory of something so small, so particular. Delicate delivery of the onomatopoeia.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、若い頃、ご親戚の稔さんと将棋を指されたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Dear, when Grandpa was young, he'd play shogi with my cousin Minoru all the time, didn't he?
lines.style: Knowing warmth. Gentle insistence — she's steering him now, coaxing out more. The 'didn't he?' lands with affectionate certainty, not doubt.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんがヤマト運輸の創業期の方々と親しかった
lines.en: Gran, when Dad was young, he was close with the people who founded Yamato Transport.
lines.style: Thoughtful, slightly proud. Slower pace on the name, honoring the connection. Reflective tone — not bragging, but acknowledging something worth remembering.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、若い頃、奥様の妹の松子さんを可愛がられたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: And when Grandpa was young, you were so fond of my sister-in-law Matsuko, weren't you?
lines.style: Warm archness in the voice. A knowing smile — she's catching him out gently. Affectionate teasing underneath the tenderness.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんが春日大社のお神札を毎年お受けされた
lines.en: Gran, when Dad was young, he'd receive a sacred charm from Kasuga Shrine every year without fail.
lines.style: Reverent, steady. Respectful pacing on the shrine name. The rhythm is almost ritual — a yearly pattern becoming a cherished habit in the telling.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、若い頃、立花流の生け花を習われたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Dear, when you were young, you learned flower arrangement in the Tachibana school, didn't you?
lines.style: Warm, intimately teasing. A small laugh waiting in the voice. She's drawn him into their shared history now — the final gentle turn that says: *I was there too.*
